title: How Your Map Finds the Fastest Way Home
sourceTitle: Dijkstra (1959), A* (1968) and contraction hierarchies (2008), explained on a code-generated city

scenes.title: You tap Home
scenes.narration: You type Home and hit Go. A moment later, there's your route. The fastest of all the ways home. How did it know?

scenes.title: A city is a graph
scenes.narration: To a computer, a city is a graph. Intersections are nodes. Streets are edges. Each edge has a weight: seconds to drive it. Corner to corner: 93 million routes. A real city has quadrillions. Checking them one by one is hopeless.

scenes.title: Amsterdam, 1956
scenes.narration: Amsterdam, 1956. Edsger Dijkstra sits down for coffee. About twenty minutes later, he has it. No pencil, no paper.

scenes.title: Closest first
scenes.narration: His trick: start at zero. Every other spot is infinity, for now. Visit the closest spot you haven't visited. Then check each of its roads. If you find a shorter way, write it down. Repeat, closest first. A visited spot is final. Roads only add time, so no detour beats it.

scenes.title: Dijkstra's ripple
scenes.narration: On a whole city, it spreads like a ripple. The moment it touches home, it's done. That's the fastest route, guaranteed.

scenes.title: A* has a sense of direction
scenes.narration: But most of that ripple went the wrong way. A-star, from 1968, adds a sense of direction. It also guesses the time left to home. Straight-line distance, at top speed. Dijkstra checked 280 intersections. A-star checked just 83, for the same route. One rule: the guess must never overestimate.

scenes.title: Traffic changes the weights
scenes.narration: Now: a crash on Central Avenue. One block now takes over two minutes. Search again, and you're around it. That's your map quietly rerouting you.

scenes.title: Continent scale
scenes.narration: Real maps: tens of millions of intersections. So routing engines do homework in advance. They precompute shortcuts. It's called contraction hierarchies. One route across Europe: under a millisecond.

scenes.title: Closest first
scenes.narration: When you're rerouted, picture the ripple. Every frame you just saw is code. And every search really ran.
